methodology: Real Three.js model hierarchy, geometry, shader materials and renderer render-list classification with production gallery-glass. Texture loader and renderer capabilities are simulated; no GPU, browser, shader compilation or performance measurement. Analytic Fresnel anchors are compared with expressions extracted from the actual shader. Actual V4 GLB geometry and resource checks are recorded separately in works-gallery-v4.json.

results.check: parent transforms, missing normals and multi-material selection bind correct native coordinates
different native meshes sharing geometry keep independent probe coordinate bindings
stage clones borrow resources and translation preserves native probe attributes and reflection directions
live theme and reflection textures remain shared; the helper owns images and the gallery owns materials
either reflection loading failure releases every successful image without replacing materials
setup failure restores assigned materials and releases images; invalid inputs never start loading
normal transform remains perpendicular under rotated and nonuniform parent transforms
Fresnel and alpha obey analytic endpoint, monotonicity and energy-weighted blending expectations
box projection agrees with independent ray-box intersections, including parallel rays on a box face
actual Three render-list classification stays transparent without transmission or renderer passes
